name: Tabata
tagline: Tokyo in 16 minutes and Otemachi in 20 minutes. Served by 2 lines. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥80,000 to ¥90,000.
summary: The station is in Kita City, where JR East run 2 lines between them. Journey times to the main business districts are 20 minutes to Otemachi, 23 minutes to Shinjuku, 28 minutes to Shibuya and 30 minutes to Shinagawa. A one-room flat rents for roughly ¥80,000 to ¥90,000. The station stands 6 m above sea level, and the ground within 800 m varies in height by 19.1 m. The land around the station has gentle slopes.

terrain.note: The station sits lower than the ground around it, at 6 m above sea level. Within 800 m the ground ranges from 3.8 m to 22.9 m, a difference of 19.1 m.

hazards: On the flood hazard map for the largest rainfall the government models, the station itself falls outside the projected inundation area. Of the nine points within 400 m of the station, 6 fall inside the area, and the deepest projection among them is 0.5 to 3 m. The projected depth differs block by block within the same station area, so check the ward hazard map for the specific address. Inland flooding from overwhelmed drains has no nationwide map; each ward publishes its own, and that is worth reading as well.

medical: Within an 800 m walk of the station there are 17 clinics and 16 pharmacies. The nearest hospital is 都立駒込病院, about 17 minutes' walk from the station. The next nearest is はせがわ病院, about 26 minutes' walk. "Hospital" here means a facility OpenStreetMap records as one. OpenStreetMap does not record whether a facility admits inpatients or which departments it runs, so check each one on its own website. For which clinics open at night and at weekends, ask the emergency advice line of the ward you live in.
stationNote: 2 lines serve the station: JR Yamanote Line and JR Keihin-Tohoku Line. Both lines are run by JR East, so a fault affecting that company can stop them together.
congestion: JR Keihin-Tohoku Line runs at 159% of capacity in the morning peak. The busiest stretch is 大井町→品川, which this station is not on. JR Yamanote Line runs at 136%. Its busiest stretch is 新大久保→新宿, which this station is likewise not on. At 150%, the ministry's scale describes shoulders not quite touching, with crowding near the doors. The figures describe each line's busiest stretch, so the stretch you ride may be easier.

rentRange.note: One room ¥80,000 to ¥90,000, 1K ¥90,000 to ¥100,000, 1LDK ¥140,000 to ¥150,000 and 2LDK ¥200,000 to ¥210,000. These are the per-station averages published by LIFULL HOME'S, Yahoo! Real Estate and at home, averaged together and rounded down to the nearest ¥10,000 (our own survey). All three are asking rents, so what tenants finally agree can be lower. Within the same station area the figure moves a great deal with the age of the building, the walk from the station, and whether the flat faces a main road.

neighbours.lead: Nishi-Nippori is ahead on the number of lines and how little of the area is in the flood projection, but Tabata is ahead on quiet.
neighbours.note: Close enough to walk to. It reaches Otemachi 7 minutes sooner than Tabata. One-room rents run about ¥7,000 higher.

leads.terrain: There are gentle slopes around the station, and which block you live on changes how much effort getting about takes.
leads.groceries: There are 12 supermarkets within walking distance, and the nearest is 2 minutes on foot.
leads.hazards: Among the 23 wards' stations, comparatively few of the points around this one fall inside the projected inundation area for the largest rainfall the government models.
leads.stationNote: 2 lines serve the station. The choice of connections is about average for the 23 wards.
leads.rentRange: Set against how long the commute takes, rents here are among the lowest in the 23 wards.
leads.medical: The number of clinics and pharmacies within walking distance is on the high side for the 23 wards.
